en: You carefully open your pack and show him your bezoar.
You show him the scar on your abdomen, and his eyes go wide.
You spend the evening with the smith going over the details until you've finally arrived at a design you're happy with.
You spend the night sleeping in the smith's bed while he spends the night working the forge.
It reads : Show that you aim ever higher.
The chunk of slag you are carrying comes to mind. Will you place the Shrike Soul upon the pedestal?
The pedestal is undamaged. There is an inscription on the very top.
You decide to hold on to the Shrike Soul for now. Perhaps it can be of use elsewhere.
You make an offering of the Shrike Soul, a bit of slag forged from the destruction of many weapons.
For a moment, it appeared as if a long, metal object flickered into existence.
The brazier has been revealed. The strange air around it is still present, but it feels like it has moved to a different part of the room...
There is a strange, cold air about this spot. You are almost certain that there is something here, but you can't see or feel it. There may be an enchantment at work.
This cabinet is full of papers and blueprints.
This lever is cold to the touch. Would you like to pull it?
With some effort, you push the lid off of the box.
Would you like to try casting a disenchantment spell?
A terrible chill runs up your spine. Something is coming.
A violent backlash of mana stings you to your core. You'll have to try again more carefully.
It looks like there is a space beneath the grate here.
Like the smaller papers before, the scroll disintegrates, as though some unseen, vindictive hand were tearing it apart.
There is a scroll positioned purposefully here. It is clearly magical, but you can make out some simple writing on the top.
There is an odd slip of paper tucked under the corner of this bed. You try to take it out to read it, but it disintegrates the moment you touch it.
There is an odd slip of paper tucked under the potted plant. You try to take it out to read it, but it disintegrates the moment you touch it.
There is an odd slip of paper tucked under the stool in the changing room. You try to take it out to read it, but it disintegrates the moment you touch it.
There is an odd slip of paper tucked under this chamber pot. You try to take it out to read it, but it disintegrates the moment you touch it.
There is an odd slip of paper tucked under this stool. You try to take it out to read it, but it disintegrates the moment you touch it.
This ladder leads to a room on the ground floor.
Those papers you found must be part of the spell's seal. You can feel the magic beginning to weaken.
You're pretty sure this wasn't here before.
A grinding noise echoes from far away.
A heavy stone cover lays on top of the chest. Attempt to move it?
A newly made wooden torch sits in the holder.
Aww... well, awright, you can pull it. But just this once!
Nobody will notice if one or two go missing...
Oi! Don't be riflin' through me laundry! That's right unhygienic, that is!
The chest contains a variety of colorful and skimpy undergarments. Do all these belong to the keysmith?
The chest is already open, but there appear to be a few coins scattered inside.
The coals radiate a pleasant warmth which fills the entire room.
The contents must have been taken somewhere else.
The water inside the barrel is cool and fresh. It's full of large, shiny red apples.
This lever is practically begging to be pulled...
This lever seems perfectly innocuous.
This may require some extra muscle.
This sack is made of finely woven jute, and is soft to the touch. You notice a few bumps, indicating that there are some items hidden inside.
You decide that it would be a good idea to close the chest, but something falls out as you do.
You manage to slide the cover off.
"Are you new? You can use the other bed if you want. We're all brothers and sisters here."
Attack Grae?
Grae slumps onto the bed, dead and bleeding into the sheets. Mother Guthrie's wish is granted.
How do you answer?
"Gerald"
A strong gust of wind sweeps away the flowers you've laid upon the headstones.
Place a flower on this headstone?
Strangely, these flowers are still healthy and strong. It appears as if they are meant to be placed upon the tombstones.
Whatever was written upon this grave is now illegible.
You take a few of the flowers.
The smell is reminiscent of the fluid you found when you started exploring Klarthus.
As you examine the odd orifice on the floor, it yawns open and swallows you!
Careful as you are to keep yourself dry, you still manage to get a bit of it on your hand. A bizarre sensation washes over you.
For a moment there is a strange sense of being connected to this place, and the whole thing suddenly feels comforting and familiar. The sensation is disturbing.
There is a pool of hot, steaming humour here. It seems unlike the rest of the foul juices that churn throughout this place.
You are deposited out of another orifice somewhere else, disturbed but otherwise unharmed.
You gingerly collect a vial of the dark, hot fluid.
It reads : This Shrine keeps my wards active and my home safe. Please do not disturb it.
Looks like someone didn't fare too well against the bear.
The chest is locked, but you decide to try the key you found on the corpse.
The remains are old, dry, and thoroughly chewed-on, but between the bones, you manage to spy a small metallic object.
The shrine has been disturbed, and its power is gone.
There are clear signs that a struggle took place here. The floor and wall near the bed have been gouged by huge claws.
There are some notes scrawled here, making reference to how to best grow mushrooms for food.
There is a small shrine here with writing carved into the lid.
These mushrooms are edible, but there are none here ripe enough to pick.
This chest is secured with a custom-built lock.
This garden is overrun with mushrooms. The are large and plump, but it's impossible to tell whether or not they are edible.
Will you disturb the shrine?
You decide to leave the shrine in peace.
You grab the body of the shrine and move it ever so slightly. An eerie chill runs through your arms, and you sense that something has changed.
You pick one of the many mushrooms growing here.
A group of bandits is closing in on some obviously terrified travelers.
A quick search turns up some items, however. It seems as though these people won't be needing them anymore.
It sounds like someone is being attacked. If you rush directly there, you might arrive in time to help whoever is in trouble.
Someone has barricaded the road, forcing travelers to take an alternate path. This barricade is quite sturdy, and it would take too long to try and dismantle it.
The ragged orc standing between the bandits and the travelers takes advantage of the momentary distraction, and swipes a knife from one of the nearby bandits.
There are a few bodies on the ground here, all with their throats freshly cut. Whoever is responsible has already disappeared.
These barrels are old and full of nothing but standing water.
This barricade looks like it was dropped hastily to trap someone inside this clearing.
This well is full of standing rainwater. It would almost certainly not be safe to drink.
There is an empty torch sconce here.
There is an empty torch sconce here. You can use your torch to light it.
The crystalline lake shimmers silently. Maybe if you find a suitable pebble, you could indulge in some rock skipping across the lake.
A crackle of errant mana surges through you. You have failed, but the ritual is still primed for another attempt.
As the dust settles and your ears stop ringing, you can hear pained voices coming from the newly exposed cells.
As you complete the ritual, the hairs on the back of your neck stand on end, and a malevolent spirit coalesces within the circle of runes!

It reads : "Bastards, all of them! I've hardly got enough room in here to think, let alone move, but I need to come up with a plan to get away from these insane cultists. Who knows what they plan to do to me?"
That was probably not supposed to happen.

The back of the note reads : "Test subjects one and three were given the blue formula. Zombification occurred within 5 hours. Two and four were given the red formula, and are ready for mana immersion."
There is a note on this corpse.
There is a ritual laid out on this scroll that appears to have something to do with the runes on the floor.
There is no response. The ritual has been spent.
There was an odd vibration. You feel a stream of mana shoot off into the distance.
This crystal appears to be powered-down. Perhaps with a source of mana, it could be activated.
You feel the mana surge and then collapse. Something is out of alignment.
You hear long string of mechanisms click in sequence somewhere to the south.
You leave the crystal alone.
"As my host led me upstairs, another striking set of nearly identical pieces only further punctuated the squalid state of this forsaken island. "
The incense burner lights, and after a couple seconds of sputtering, holds itself. Just outside the room, you hear some heavy stone grinding on wood.
The incense burner you tried to light appears to hold for a second, but then magically goes out. There seems to be some interference coming from somewhere else on the floor.
The water in this bird bath is murky with algae and who knows what else.
You see some glittering objects in the water at the bottom of the bird bath. After scooping around the liquid a bit, you find a small sum of coins to add to your pouch.
The cog fits inside neatly, and you hear a click from the door nearby and from behind the bookshelves to the right.
There is a large hole in the center of this panel. It looks like something is supposed to fit inside.
There is a large hole in the centre of this panel. It looks like the cog you found would fit inside.
There was a strange noise from somewhere else, perhaps closer toward the entrance.
The old woman whistles a brief note, her face twisted into an inhuman grin.
The woman's tone is well-practiced and syrupy-sweet. "Why hello, deary," she says. "I'm just putting a fresh log on the fire. Come on in and make yourself at home."
These barrels have been set here as a crude barricade, but they are empty and could be easily moved.
It looks like you've cut down all of the trees in the stand. You return the axe to the stump.
Paul grabs the haft of the axe and effortlessly hauls it out of the tree stump.
There is a woodcutter's axe lodged in the stump here.
Will you try to cut down a tree?
You spend some time felling a tree.
Empty.
Inspecting the chest, you find it void of contents.
Searching through the chests again, nothing has changed. Nothing to be found.
You find something in the chest here... some twigs and leaves.
A serious expression takes over Logus' face as he looks up at you.
Captain Logus sits here on the edge of the bed, clutching at his side. He has bandaged himself, but he is not looking well.
Give the Golden Philter to Logus?
Logus gingerly peels away his bandages, revealing his smooth, rugged flank unmarred by injury. He whistles and slaps the bare skin.
Logus laughs a bit, and then winces, obviously in pain.
The beacon appears to be magical in nature, but there is currently no mana powering it. Someone with appropriate training might be able to restart it.
The beacon flickers to life, its facets shining brightly through the barred windows. This lighthouse should now be visible from a very great distance away.
There is ample mana present, but you didn't manage to align it with the crystal. Another attempt may be in order.
These stairs are too steep and narrow for you to traverse them more than one at a time.
This beacon is gleaming brightly. There is enough ambient mana in the lighthouse to keep it lit for several weeks at least.
You hand the Golden Philter to Logus, and he carefully uncorks it and downs it, careful not to spill a drop.

"How do you feel?" he asks. 
It is hard to remember having felt better in recent memory. You thank him and collect your things.

"I'm sorry, I don't have any potions for sale right now. You should go to the market if you need something. There's a lovely woman who-"):

After taking stock of you, she retreats back to her position at the intersection.
An armed woman at the gate steps forward and bars your path. She hasn't drawn a blade, but she is clearly ready to.
An inscription along the base reads : Honour the insects, and they will guide you to a bountiful harvest.

As he works the last of the powder into the spaces between your toes, he looks up at you and smiles. "Everyone here has a story, and now you know mine. My days of killing are long behind me, but I am pleased to have been of some service to you."
For the last little while, you've been browsing the modest marketplace on your own.

He lights a few pleasant-smelling candles and whispers close to your ear, urging you to close your eyes and let yourself vanish into his hands. It is difficult not to. Time seems to slow to a crawl, and the world fades to nothing but a pair of powerful hands folding your flesh like soft clay.
How much do you want to tip him?
In the morning, you are feeling right as rain, with only the barest scar to show for your agonizing trial.
In the morning, you reconvene with your party, and prepare for another day on the road.
It is, however, too late for second thoughts. You adjust your posture and grit your teeth.
It sounds like getting one of these stones is going to be a bad time.
It's been an easy day, and when you arrive in town, you tell the rest of your party to relax.

Over the next hour, he works over every inch of your road-weary body, and it feels like the weight of the world is leaking out through your pores. When he seems to be finished, he fetches a jar of some kind of powder and begins to sprinkle it over your naked body.
That strikes you as an excellent idea. You close your eyes and drift off again.
The chunk of slag you are carrying comes to mind. Will you place the Mantis Soul upon the statue?
The healer hands you a wide glass full of a yellowish fluid.

The man lays you on the table and begins to massage a warm scented oil into your back. His hands are large and strong, and he does as he promised, pressing into your skin and grasping at the aches in your muscles. He seems to know exactly where to touch in order to make your pain melt away.
The old healer grinds powders and pastes together and eventually presents you with a potion that smells like it was brewed in the armpit of an ogre.
The old healer grins, his chipped tusks cutting through his gnarled beard.
The potion also tastes like it was brewed in the armpit of an ogre. It takes a moment for you to stop gagging.
There is a statue of a woman with a jug of water. Based on what you can see here, she is the patron saint of the harvest.
This crate is full of bottles of a deep red liquid. The bottles are frosted with condensation, and are clearly very cold.
This table is laid out with a variety of piping-hot foodstuffs, presumably prepared by the buxom woman nearby.
Time seems to slow to a crawl, and the world fades to nothing but a pair of powerful hands folding your flesh like soft clay.

When he is finished, he stands and dusts off his hands. His skin is glistening with sweat - obviously this was no small effort for him. You, on the other hand, feel reborn. You collect your things and thank him earnestly.

When he is finished, he stands and dusts off his hands. His skin is glistening with sweat - obviously this was no small effort for him. You, on the other hand, feel reborn. You collect your things and thank him earnestly. He clasps your hand respectfully and ushers you back out into the room.
With an impossibly gentle touch, he rubs the powder into your skin, from your neck to the spaces between your toes. It has an appealing smell and leaves your skin soft and tingling.

You ask him about his techniques as he softly begins to rub the powder into your neck. He seems like he is going to protest, but you feel his thumb rub over your brand, and he sighs softly. "I don't normally talk about that, but you've been most generous, so I suppose you deserve to know."

You come to your senses gradually with the man's huge hands lightly stroking your neck and shoulders. Considering how easily he pushed through your flesh before, his touch is impossibly delicate. He reaches for a towel and gently wipes the oil from your skin.
You decide to hold on to the Mantis Soul for now. Perhaps it can be of use elsewhere.
You get the sense that he knows this from personal experience, but before you can ask, he speaks again.
You make an offering of the Mantis Soul, a bit of slag forged from the destruction of many weapons.

You reach down to your purse on the floor and shovel out a large handful of coins toward the Masseur. His eyes go wide and he laughs. "You must be impressed with me indeed. For that, I'll use every technique I know. Perhaps you should tell your friends to browse. We may be a while."

You reach down to your purse on the floor and slip a few extra coins out, nudging them toward the Masseur. He smiles and collects them in a cup, nodding appreciatively. Time seems to slow to a crawl, and the world fades to nothing but a pair of powerful hands folding your flesh like soft clay.
You spend the night in town, and the rest of your visit to Marsaven is uneventful.
You still feel a dull pain in your gut, but the pressure is gone, and you know that the stone has been removed.
You've had a mind to find a gift for Nazar, but nothing they have for sale here has caught your eye, and you've nearly given up on the idea.
Your head throbs as the world lazily pours back into your eyes.
Your party spent the night in town, and your evening in particular was most uncomfortable. There is already a pressure in the pit of your gut that was not there yesterday.
As you were trekking through the marsh, you were caught by surprise in a goblin ambush.
Borf is badly hurt, but the bleeding is under control. You bundle up his small body in a cloak to keep him warm and dry, and set about carrying him back to the stronghold.
Borfalgor is in a very delicate emotional state right now.
Borfalgor is sadly surveying the blood and mud-covered corpses of the goblin attackers.
Borfalgor opens his mouth to reply, but nothing comes out, and he just stands in the rain staring at the ground.
He takes a sharp breath as you tie the bandage tightly about his chest. For a moment, he seems like he is going to speak, but instead he just grasps for your hand and squeezes it appreciateively.
The corner of Borfalgor's mouth creeps up in a restrained smile, and he sighs heavily.
There are quite a few of them, and they seem unbothered by the muddy terrain, so they were able to surround you in a matter of moments.
You begin tearing up Borfalgor's clothes to make some temporary bandages for his wounds, and he looks at you sadly.
You search through the muck, and among the dead and dying goblins, you find Borfalgor. He is badly bleeding, but still breathing.
As you return to the gatehouse together, Nazar walks close beside you, beaming in the morning light.
Before you know it, dawn is upon you, morning sun beaming in through the crumbling ceiling. You haven't slept at all, but you feel relaxed, and the horrors of the island seem very far away.
Eventually, the water stops flowing, and the two of you head back to the gatehouse together, settling back into your beds for what's left of the night.
He raises his hand to you slowly, and rubs his thumb along the side of your face.
It is obvious that last night was very special to him.
It looks like this may have once been a large kitchen, but it clearly hasn't been used in a very long time.
It seems you're in for an interesting night.
It's a water tower. Though ancient and leaky, it still has a decent reserve of water, probably from recent rainfall.
It's far too old to light.
More footprints sprawl through the barracks, approaching many of the rotting cots before moving on.
Nazar can take care of himself, and if he wants some privacy, surely he's entitled to it. You decide to go back to bed.
Nazar fingers your beard affectionately, his eyes transfixing yours as he leans closer.
Nazar gives you a half-cocked grin and stands up.
Nazar is being coy.
Nazar puts his arms around you and kisses you, pulling your body tight against his.
Nazar rests his head on your shoulder and hotly whispers against your neck.
Nazar seems a little disappointed, but he nods.
Nazar seems rather pleased with himself.
Nazar smiles and lowers his head a little, embarassed.
Nazar throws himself against you, your chests and mouths colliding in the wet darkness.
Nazar turns a small valve on the nearby pipe.
Nazar's face is split with a delighted grin as he takes a slow step toward you.
Some kind of valve. It appears to have been opened recently. You can hear water gurgling through the nearby pipes.
That noise was definitely not Nazar.
The building appears to be Tsarathi, probably built by orcs for use by orcs.
The building is an utter ruin, but there's nowhere else he could be. He must have gone inside.
The footprints lead to this door.
The place is an utter ruin, with most of the ceiling laying in pieces on the floor.
The room is lit by the glow of this furnace. It must have been lit recently.
The water looks clean and inviting.
There are fresh footprints in the grime that covers the floor.
There is a gurgling noise coming from nearby.
This access will be disabled later.
This furnace is cold and mouldering. There's no fuel nearby to light it.
This gate appears to be badly seized. It would be easy enough to climb it, but without easy access, the area beyond would be worthless as a stronghold.
This looks like it used to be a communal living area for soldiers.
When you wake up to the morning sun, Nazar is still yawning and shaking the sleep out of his body. It seems he didn't go far after all.
When you wake up to the morning sun, Nazar is still yawning and shaking the sleep out of his body. It seems he made it back without incident.
When you wake up to the morning sun, Nazar is still yawning and shaking the sleep out of his body. You missed out on a few hours sleep, but the hot shower was absolutely worth it.
You and Nazar chat in the shower for hours, getting to know one another in a place that seems, for once, far-removed from the horrors of Lukatt.
You cling to Nazar all through the night. The hours go by in a haze of wet skin and urgent whispers, the water pounding in your head as you explore ways to fit your mouths and bodies together.
